sentences.zh: 金自景祖始建官屬，統諸部以專征伐，嶷然自為一國。

translations.literal: From the time of Emperor Jingzu, the Jin established official staff, unified the tribes for exclusive military campaigns, and stood forth distinctly as a separate state.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Jingzu onward the Jin built up a corps of officials, united the tribes under a single command for warfare, and thus emerged unmistakably as a state in its own right.

sentences.zh: 其官長皆稱曰勃極烈，故太祖以都勃極烈嗣位，太宗以諳版勃極烈居守。

translations.literal: All their chiefs were styled bojilie; therefore the Founder succeeded to the succession as Chief Bojilie, and Taizong served as Guardian with the rank of Anban Bojilie.
translations.idiomatic: Their leaders were all called bojilie; thus the Founder inherited rule as Chief Bojilie, while Taizong held the capital as Guardian Bojilie.

sentences.zh: 諳版，尊大之稱也。

translations.literal: "Anban" is a title of lofty respect.
translations.idiomatic: Anban was an honorific of the highest dignity.

sentences.zh: 其次曰國論忽魯勃極烈，國論言貴，忽魯猶總帥也。

translations.literal: Next came the Guolun Hurulu Bojilie; "guolun" means noble, and "hurulu" is like commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Below that stood the Guolun Hurulu Bojilie—guolun meaning "noble," hurulu the equivalent of a supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 又有國論勃極烈，或左右置，所謂國相也。

translations.literal: There were also Guolun Bojilie, placed to left or right—what were called state chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the Guolun Bojilie, installed to left and right—the office known as state chancellor.

sentences.zh: 其次諸勃極烈之上，則有國論、乙室、忽魯、移賚、阿買、阿舍、昊、迭之號，以為升拜宗室功臣之序焉。

translations.literal: Above the various bojilie in rank were the titles Guolun, Yishi, Hurulu, Yicai, Amai, Ashe, Hao, and Die, serving as the sequence for promoting imperial clansmen and meritorious officials.
translations.idiomatic: Higher still were the ranks Guolun, Yishi, Hurulu, Yicai, Amai, Ashe, Hao, and Die—the ladder by which clansmen and meritorious servants were advanced.

sentences.zh: 其部長曰孛堇，統數部者曰忽魯。

translations.literal: Their tribal chiefs were called bojin; those who commanded several tribes were called hurulu.
translations.idiomatic: A tribal chief was styled bojin; one who ruled several tribes was called hurulu.

sentences.zh: 凡此，至熙宗定官制皆廢。

translations.literal: All of these were abolished when Emperor Xizong fixed the official system.
translations.idiomatic: All of these offices were swept away when Emperor Xizong established the formal bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 其後惟鎮撫邊民之官曰禿裏，烏魯骨之下有掃穩脫朵，詳穩之下有麼忽、習尼昆，此則具於官制而不廢，皆踵遼官名也。

translations.literal: Thereafter only the office for pacifying border peoples called tuli remained; under ulugu were saowen tuoduo, and under xiangwen were mohu and xinikun—these are set out in the official regulations and were not abolished, all following Liao official titles.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward only the border-pacification post called tuli survived; beneath the ulugu stood the saowen tuoduo, and beneath the xiangwen the mohu and xinikun—these remained codified in the bureaucracy and were not abolished, all titles inherited from the Liao.

sentences.zh: 漢官之制，自平州人不樂為猛安謀克之官，始置長吏以下。

translations.literal: The Han official system began when the people of Pingzhou, unwilling to serve as meng'an and mouke officers, first had regular administrators and subordinates appointed.
translations.idiomatic: The Han bureaucracy began when Pingzhou subjects, reluctant to hold meng'an and mouke posts, were first given regular magistrates and their subordinates.

sentences.zh: 天輔七年以左企弓行樞密院于廣甯，尚踵遼南院之舊。

translations.literal: In Tianfu 7 (1123) Zuo Qigong directed the Bureau of Military Affairs at Guangning, still following the old Liao Southern Commission model.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu year 7 Zuo Qigong ran the Bureau of Military Affairs at Guangning, still on the pattern of the Liao Southern Commission.

sentences.zh: 天會四年，建尚書省，遂有三省之制。

translations.literal: In Tianhui 4 (1126) the Imperial Secretariat was established, and thus the Three Departments system came into being.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui year 4 the Imperial Secretariat was founded, giving the state the Three Departments framework.

sentences.zh: 至熙宗頒新官制及換官格，除拜內外官，始定勳封食邑入銜，而後其制定。

translations.literal: When Xizong promulgated the new official system and the regulations for changing offices, appointing inner and outer officials, and first fixing enfeoffment of merit, fiefs, and stipendiary estates in titles—the system was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xizong the new bureaucracy and transfer regulations were issued; appointments of central and local officials were made, titles of merit, fiefs, and stipendiary estates were standardized in rank designations—and only then was the system complete.

sentences.zh: 然大率皆循遼、宋之舊。

translations.literal: Yet for the most part it all followed the old models of Liao and Song.
translations.idiomatic: For the most part, however, it followed Liao and Song precedents.

sentences.zh: 海陵庶人正隆元年罷中書門下省，止置尚書省。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenglong (1156), the Commoner of Hailing abolished the Secretariat and Chancellery, retaining only the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenglong year 1 the usurper Hailing abolished the Secretariat and Chancellery, leaving only the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 自省而下官司之別，曰院、曰台、曰府、曰司、曰寺、曰監、曰局、曰署、曰所，各統其屬以修其職。

translations.literal: Below the Secretariat the offices were distinguished as yuan, tai, fu, si, si (temple), jian, ju, shu, and suo, each governing its subordinates to perform its duties.
translations.idiomatic: Beneath the Secretariat the agencies were divided into yuan, tai, fu, si, temples, jian, ju, shu, and suo—each supervising its staff to carry out its functions.

sentences.zh: 職有定位，員有常數，紀綱明，庶務舉，是以終金之世守而不敢變焉。

translations.literal: Each post had a fixed place, each office a set quota; regulations were clear and routine affairs were handled—therefore through the entire Jin age they were maintained and none dared alter them.
translations.idiomatic: Every post had its place and every office its quota; discipline was clear and business ran smoothly—so for the whole Jin dynasty the system was kept intact and no one dared change it.

sentences.zh: 大定二十八年，在仕官一萬九千七百員，四季赴選者千餘，歲數監差者三千。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Dading (1188), serving officials numbered 19,700; over a thousand came each season for selection, and about three thousand were dispatched on supervisory assignments each year.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading year 28 there were 19,700 officials in service; each season more than a thousand presented themselves for appointment, and some three thousand received supervisory commissions annually.

sentences.zh: 明昌四年奏，周歲，官死及事故者六百七十，新入仕者五百一十，見在官萬一千四百九十九，內女直四千七百五員，漢人六千七百九十四員。

translations.literal: A memorial in the fourth year of Mingchang (1193) reported that over the year 670 officials died or left office through mishap, 510 newly entered service, and 11,499 remained in office—of whom 4,705 were Jurchen and 6,794 were Han.
translations.idiomatic: A Mingchang year 4 report noted that over the past year 670 officials had died or left through mishap, 510 had newly entered service, and 11,499 remained on the rolls—4,705 Jurchen and 6,794 Han.

sentences.zh: 至泰和七年，在仕官四萬七千餘，四季部擬授者千七百，監官到部者九千二百九十餘，則三倍世宗之時矣。

translations.literal: By the seventh year of Taihe (1207), serving officials exceeded 47,000; 1,700 were drafted for appointment each season by the ministries, and over 9,290 supervisory officials reached the ministries—three times the number in Shizong's day.
translations.idiomatic: By Taihe year 7 more than 47,000 officials were in service; the ministries drafted 1,700 appointments each season, and over 9,290 supervisory officers reported to the capital—three times the figure under Emperor Shizong.

sentences.zh: 若宣宗之招賢所、經略司，義宗之益政院，雖危亡之政亦必列於其次，以著一時之事雲。

translations.literal: Such institutions as Emperor Xuanzong's Office for Recruiting Talent and the Pacification Commission, and Emperor Yizong's Bureau for Benefiting Government—even policies of a dying age—are listed below to record affairs of their time.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong's Office for Recruiting Talent and Pacification Commission, and Emperor Yizong's Bureau for Benefiting Government—even institutions of a dynasty in collapse—are recorded below to mark what belonged to each reign.

sentences.zh: 太師、太傅、太保各一員，皆正一品。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Guardian—one each, all of the first positive rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Guardian—one post each, all at the first positive rank.

sentences.zh: 師範一人，儀刑四海。

translations.literal: A single model for instruction, the standard of conduct for all within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: A lone exemplar of learning, the moral pattern for the realm.

sentences.zh: 太尉、司徒、司空各一員，皆正一品。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant, Minister of Education, and Minister of Works—one each, all of the first positive rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant, Minister of Education, and Minister of Works—one post each, all at the first positive rank.

sentences.zh: 論道經邦，燮理陰陽。

translations.literal: They discourse on the Way and govern the state, harmonizing yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: They counsel on the Way, steer the state, and harmonize the forces of yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 尚書省

translations.literal: Imperial Secretariat
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Secretariat

sentences.zh: 尚書令一員，正一品。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat—one post, first positive rank.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat—one post, first positive rank.

sentences.zh: 總領紀綱，儀刑端揆。

translations.literal: He oversees all regulations and is the model for the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He presides over the entire administrative code and sets the standard for the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 左丞相、右丞相各一員，從一品。

translations.literal: Left and Right Chancellors—one each, first secondary rank.
translations.idiomatic: Left and Right Chancellor—one each, first secondary rank.

sentences.zh: 平章政事二員，從一品。

translations.literal: Commissioners with Full Authority—two posts, first secondary rank.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioners with Full Authority—two posts, first secondary rank.

sentences.zh: 為宰相，掌丞天子，平章萬機。

translations.literal: They serve as chancellors, assisting the Son of Heaven and deliberating on all affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellors they assist the Son of Heaven and deliberate on every matter of government.

sentences.zh: 左丞、右丞各一員，正二品。

translations.literal: Left and Right Vice Chancellors—one each, second positive rank.
translations.idiomatic: Left and Right Vice Chancellor—one each, second positive rank.

sentences.zh: 參知政事二員，從二品。

translations.literal: Participating Administrators—two posts, second secondary rank.
translations.idiomatic: Participating Administrators—two posts, second secondary rank.

sentences.zh: 為執政官，為宰相之貳，佐治省事。

translations.literal: They are executive officials, deputies to the chancellors, assisting in the governance of secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: They are executive officers, second to the chancellors, and help administer secretariat business.

sentences.zh: 左司，郎中一員，正五品。

translations.literal: Left Bureau: one Director, fifth positive rank.
translations.idiomatic: Left Bureau: one Director at the fifth positive rank.

sentences.zh: 國初置左、右司侍郎，天眷三年始更今名。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state Left and Right Bureau Vice Directors were appointed; in Tianjuan 3 (1140) the present title was first adopted.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding the posts were Left and Right Bureau Vice Directors; in Tianjuan year 3 they received their present titles.

sentences.zh: 舊凡視朝，執政官親執奏，自天德二年詔以付左、右司官，為定制。

translations.literal: Formerly at every court audience the executive officials personally presented memorials; from Tiande 2 (1150) an edict assigned this to the Left and Right Bureau officers, and it became standard practice.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly at court audiences the executive ministers presented memorials in person; from Tiande year 2 onward an edict entrusted this duty to the Left and Right Bureau officers, and that became fixed practice.

sentences.zh: 員外郎一員，正六品。

translations.literal: Associate Director—one post, sixth positive rank.
translations.idiomatic: Associate Director—one post, sixth positive rank.

sentences.zh: 掌本司奏事，總察吏、戶、禮三部受事付事，兼帶修起居注官，回避其間記述之事。

translations.literal: He manages this bureau's memorials to the throne, oversees receipt and dispatch of business for the Personnel, Revenue, and Rites ministries, and concurrently holds the post of recorder of the imperial diary, recusing himself from matters he records.
translations.idiomatic: He handles the bureau's presentations to the throne, supervises intake and routing for the Personnel, Revenue, and Rites ministries, and also serves as diarist—recusing himself from anything he must record.

sentences.zh: 每月朔朝，則先集是月秩滿者為簿，名曰闕本，及行止簿、貼黃簿、並官制同進呈，御覽畢則受而藏之。

translations.literal: At the first court audience each month he first compiles a register of those whose terms expire that month, called the Vacancy Register, together with the Conduct Register, the Yellow-Slip Register, and the official regulations—all presented together; after imperial review they are received and filed.
translations.idiomatic: At the first audience of each month he first assembles a list of officers whose terms expire that month—the Vacancy Register—along with the Conduct Register, the Yellow-Slip Register, and the code of offices; all are presented together, and after the emperor has reviewed them they are filed away.

sentences.zh: 每有除拜，凡尚書省所不敢擬注者，則一闕具二三人以聽制授焉。

translations.literal: Whenever an appointment is made, for any post the Secretariat dares not draft a nomination, one vacancy is furnished with two or three names for the emperor to choose and appoint.
translations.idiomatic: For any appointment the Secretariat itself would not dare to nominate, two or three candidates are listed for a single vacancy and the emperor chooses whom to appoint.

sentences.zh: 都事二員，正七品。

translations.literal: Chief Clerks—two posts, seventh positive rank.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerks—two posts, seventh positive rank.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，左右司官，宮中出身，並進士、令史三色人內通選。

translations.literal: In Zhenyuan 2 (1154), Left and Right Bureau officers were chosen broadly from palace-trained staff, examination graduates, and secretariat clerks.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan year 2 Left and Right Bureau officers were selected from palace-trained staff, jinshi degree-holders, and secretariat clerks alike.

sentences.zh: 三年，以監察禦史相應人取次稟奏，不復擬注。

translations.literal: In the third year, suitable censorate investigators were reported in order to the throne for appointment, and draft nominations ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 suitable censorate investigators were reported to the throne in turn for appointment, and the Secretariat no longer drafted nominations.

sentences.zh: 掌本司受事付事，檢勾稽失、省署文牘，兼知省內宿直，檢校架閣等事。

translations.literal: They manage receipt and dispatch for this bureau, audit errors, review secretariat documents, and also oversee night duty within the Secretariat and inspection of the archive shelves.
translations.idiomatic: They handle the bureau's intake and routing, audit for errors, review secretariat paperwork, oversee night duty in the Secretariat, and inspect the archive.

sentences.zh: 右司所掌同。

translations.literal: The Right Bureau's duties are the same.
translations.idiomatic: The Right Bureau's responsibilities are identical.

sentences.zh: 右司，郎中一員，正五品。

translations.literal: Right Bureau: one Director, fifth positive rank.
translations.idiomatic: Right Bureau: one Director at the fifth positive rank.

sentences.zh: 員外郎一員，正六品。

translations.literal: Associate Director—one post, sixth positive rank.
translations.idiomatic: Associate Director—one post, sixth positive rank.

sentences.zh: 掌本司奏事，總察兵、刑、工三部受事付事，兼帶修注官，回避其間記述之事。

translations.literal: He manages this bureau's memorials, oversees receipt and dispatch for the War, Justice, and Works ministries, and concurrently holds the diarist post, recusing himself from matters he records.
translations.idiomatic: He handles the bureau's presentations, supervises intake and routing for the War, Justice, and Works ministries, and also serves as diarist—recusing himself from anything he must record.

sentences.zh: 都事二員，正七品。

translations.literal: Chief Clerks—two posts, seventh positive rank.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerks—two posts, seventh positive rank.

sentences.zh: 尚書省祗候郎君管勾官，從七品。

translations.literal: Secretariat Attendant Escort Controller—seventh secondary rank.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Attendant Escort Controller—seventh secondary rank.

sentences.zh: 掌祗候郎君，謹其出入及差遣之事。

translations.literal: He manages the attendant escorts, supervising their comings and goings and assignments.
translations.idiomatic: He supervises the attendant escorts, regulating their movements and assignments.

sentences.zh: 承安二年以前，走馬郎君擬注。

translations.literal: Before Chengan 2 (1197), draft appointments went to mounted escorts.
translations.idiomatic: Before Chengan year 2 the post was filled by draft nomination of mounted escorts.

sentences.zh: 《泰和令》，以左右女直都事兼。

translations.literal: The Taihe Statutes provide that Left and Right Jurchen Chief Clerks hold it concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Taihe Statutes the Left and Right Jurchen Chief Clerks hold the post concurrently.

sentences.zh: 正大間，改用親從人。

translations.literal: During the Zhengda period (1224–1234), close attendants of the emperor were used instead.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengda era the post was filled by the emperor's personal attendants.

sentences.zh: 架閣庫大定二十一年六月設，仍以都事提控之。

translations.literal: The Archive Repository was established in the sixth month of Dading 21 (1181), still supervised by the Chief Clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The Archive Repository was founded in the sixth month of Dading year 21 and remained under Chief Clerk supervision.

sentences.zh: 管勾舊二員，正大省一員，正八品。

translations.literal: Controllers—formerly two posts; under Zhengda reduced to one, eighth positive rank.
translations.idiomatic: Controllers—formerly two; under Zhengda reduced to one at the eighth positive rank.

sentences.zh: 同管勾舊二員，正大省一員，從八品。

translations.literal: Associate Controllers—formerly two posts; under Zhengda reduced to one, eighth secondary rank.
translations.idiomatic: Associate Controllers—formerly two; under Zhengda reduced to one at the eighth secondary rank.

sentences.zh: 總掌察左右司大程官追付文牘，並提控小都監給受紙筆，余管勾同。

translations.literal: They oversee pursuit of documents from senior Left and Right Bureau clerks and supervise junior controllers in issuing paper and brushes; other duties match those of the controllers.
translations.idiomatic: They track down documents from senior Left and Right Bureau clerks and supervise junior controllers in distributing stationery; their other duties match those of the controllers.

sentences.zh: 女直省令史三十五人，左二十人，右十五人。

translations.literal: Jurchen secretariat clerks—35 in all: 20 on the left, 15 on the right.
translations.idiomatic: Jurchen secretariat clerks—35 in all: 20 on the left, 15 on the right.

sentences.zh: 大定二十四年為三十人，進士十人，宰執子、宗室子十人，密院台部統軍司令史十人。

translations.literal: In Dading 24 (1184) the quota was 30: ten jinshi, ten sons of chief ministers and imperial clansmen, and ten clerks from the Military Affairs Bureau, Censorate, ministries, and commandery headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading year 24 the quota was set at 30: ten jinshi, ten sons of chief ministers and clansmen, and ten clerks drawn from the Military Affairs Bureau, Censorate, ministries, and army commands.

sentences.zh: 漢令史三十五人，左二十一人、右十四人。

translations.literal: Han secretariat clerks—35 in all: 21 on the left, 14 on the right.
translations.idiomatic: Han secretariat clerks—35 in all: 21 on the left, 14 on the right.

sentences.zh: 省譯史十四人，左右各七人。

translations.literal: Secretariat translators—14 in all, seven on each side.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat translators—14 in all, seven on each side.

sentences.zh: 女直譯史同。

translations.literal: Jurchen translators—the same number.
translations.idiomatic: Jurchen translators—the same quota.

sentences.zh: 通事八人，左右各四人。

translations.literal: Interpreters—eight in all, four on each side.
translations.idiomatic: Interpreters—eight in all, four on each side.

sentences.zh: 高麗、夏國、回紇譯史四人，左右各二人。

translations.literal: Translators for Koryo, Western Xia, and Uyghur—four in all, two on each side.
translations.idiomatic: Translators for Koryŏ, Western Xia, and Uyghur—four in all, two on each side.

sentences.zh: 諸部通事六人。

translations.literal: Tribal interpreters—six in all.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal interpreters—six in all.

sentences.zh: 曳剌二十人。

translations.literal: Yela runners—twenty in all.
translations.idiomatic: Yela couriers—twenty in all.

sentences.zh: 走馬郎君五十人。

translations.literal: Mounted escorts—fifty in all.
translations.idiomatic: Mounted escorts—fifty in all.

sentences.zh: 提點歲賜所，左右司郎中，員外郎兼之，掌提點歲賜出入錢幣之事。

translations.literal: Office for Overseeing Annual Grants: held concurrently by the Left and Right Bureau Directors and Associate Directors, managing disbursement and receipt of annual grant monies.
translations.idiomatic: Office for Overseeing Annual Grants: held concurrently by the Left and Right Bureau Directors and Associate Directors, which supervises the issue and receipt of annual stipend monies.

sentences.zh: 堂食公使酒庫。

translations.literal: Hall Provisions and Envoy Wine Storehouse
translations.idiomatic: Hall Provisions and Envoy Wine Storehouse

sentences.zh: 使一員，從八品。

translations.literal: Commissioner—one post, eighth secondary rank.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner—one post, eighth secondary rank.

sentences.zh: 掌受給歲賜錢，總領庫事。

translations.literal: He receives and disburses annual grant funds and oversees all storehouse affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He receives and disburses annual grant funds and oversees the storehouse.

sentences.zh: 副一員，正九品。

translations.literal: Deputy—one post, ninth positive rank.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy—one post, ninth positive rank.

sentences.zh: 掌貳使事。

translations.literal: He assists the commissioner in his duties.
translations.idiomatic: He assists the commissioner.

sentences.zh: 直省局。

translations.literal: Direct Secretariat Bureau
translations.idiomatic: Direct Secretariat Bureau

sentences.zh: 局長，從八品。

translations.literal: Bureau Chief—eighth secondary rank.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau Chief—eighth secondary rank.

sentences.zh: 掌都堂之禮及官員參謝之儀。

translations.literal: He manages ceremonial at the chief hall and the rites of officials' audience and thanksgiving.
translations.idiomatic: He oversees ceremony in the chief hall and the protocol for officials' audiences and leave-taking.

sentences.zh: 副局長，正九品，掌貳局長。

translations.literal: Deputy Bureau Chief—ninth positive rank, assisting the Bureau Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Bureau Chief—ninth positive rank, assisting the Bureau Chief.

sentences.zh: 管勾尚書省樂工，從九品。

translations.literal: Controller of Secretariat Musicians—ninth secondary rank.
translations.idiomatic: Controller of Secretariat Musicians—ninth secondary rank.

sentences.zh: 國初與左、右司通署，天眷三年始分治。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state it shared offices with the Left and Right Bureaus; in Tianjuan 3 (1140) separate administration began.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding it shared quarters with the Left and Right Bureaus; in Tianjuan year 3 it received its own administration.

sentences.zh: 尚書一員，正三品。

translations.literal: Minister—one post, third positive rank.
translations.idiomatic: Minister—one post, third positive rank.

sentences.zh: 侍郎一員，正四品。

translations.literal: Vice Minister—one post, fourth positive rank.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister—one post, fourth positive rank.

sentences.zh: 郎中二員，從五品。

translations.literal: Directors—two posts, fifth secondary rank.
translations.idiomatic: Directors—two posts, fifth secondary rank.

sentences.zh: 天德二年，增作四員，後省。

translations.literal: In Tiande 2 (1150) increased to four posts; later reduced.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiande year 2 the quota was raised to four; later it was cut back.

sentences.zh: 員外郎，從六品。

translations.literal: Associate Director—sixth secondary rank.
translations.idiomatic: Associate Director—sixth secondary rank.

sentences.zh: 天德二年，增作四員，後省。

translations.literal: In Tiande 2 (1150) increased to four posts; later reduced.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiande year 2 the quota was raised to four; later it was cut back.

sentences.zh: 掌文武選授、勳封、考課、出給制誥之政。

translations.literal: It governs civil and military selection and appointment, enfeoffment for merit, performance review, and issuance of patents of appointment.
translations.idiomatic: It governs civil and military appointments, enfeoffment for merit, performance reviews, and the issue of patents of office.

sentences.zh: 以才行勞效，比仕者之賢否；

translations.literal: By ability, conduct, and meritorious service it compares the fitness of office-seekers;
translations.idiomatic: By talent, conduct, and service it judges whether candidates are fit for office;

sentences.zh: 以行止、文冊、貼黃簿，制名闕之機要。

translations.literal: by the Conduct Register, document files, and Yellow-Slip Register it controls the essentials of filling named vacancies.
translations.idiomatic: and through the Conduct Register, personnel files, and Yellow-Slip Register it controls the machinery for filling named vacancies.

sentences.zh: 正七品以上，以名上省，聽制授。

translations.literal: For the seventh positive rank and above, names are sent up to the Secretariat and appointments await imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: From the seventh positive rank upward, names go to the Secretariat and await the emperor's appointment.

sentences.zh: 從七品以下，每至季月則循資格而擬注，自八品以上則奏，以下則否。

translations.literal: For the seventh secondary rank and below, at each season's end draft nominations follow seniority rules; from the eighth rank upward they are reported to the throne, below that they are not.
translations.idiomatic: From the seventh secondary rank down, draft nominations each season follow seniority rules; from the eighth rank up they are reported to the throne, below that they are not.

sentences.zh: 侍郎以下，皆為尚書之貳。

translations.literal: From the Vice Minister down, all are deputies to the Minister.
translations.idiomatic: From the Vice Minister down, all serve as the Minister's deputies.

sentences.zh: 郎中掌文武選、流外遷用、官吏差使、行止名簿、封爵制誥。

translations.literal: The Directors manage civil and military selection, promotion of non-regular clerks, official assignments, conduct registers, ennoblement, and patents.
translations.idiomatic: The Directors handle civil and military selection, promotion of non-regular clerks, official assignments, conduct registers, ennoblement, and patents of appointment.

sentences.zh: 一員掌勳級酬賞、承襲用廕、循遷、致仕、考課、議諡之事。

translations.literal: One Director manages grades of merit and rewards, hereditary succession and use of yin privilege, routine transfers, retirement, performance review, and deliberation on posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: One Director oversees merit grades and rewards, hereditary succession and yin privilege, routine transfers, retirement, performance reviews, and deliberation on posthumous titles.

sentences.zh: 員外郎分判曹務及參議事，所掌與郎中同。

translations.literal: Associate Directors divide departmental duties and participate in deliberation; their responsibilities match those of the Directors.
translations.idiomatic: Associate Directors divide departmental business and join deliberations; their duties match those of the Directors.

sentences.zh: 文官九品，階凡四十有二：從一品上曰開府儀同三司，中曰儀同三司，中次曰特進，下曰崇進。

translations.literal: Civil officials of nine ranks have forty-two grades in all: at the top of the first secondary rank, Superior Opening the Government with Equal Ceremony to the Three Dukes; in the middle, Equal Ceremony to the Three Dukes; next below, Special Advancement; at the bottom, Honored Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials of nine ranks have forty-two grades: at the top of the first secondary rank stands Superior Opening the Government with Equal Ceremony to the Three Dukes; in the middle, Equal Ceremony to the Three Dukes; next below, Special Advancement; at the bottom, Honored Advancement.

sentences.zh: 正二品上曰金紫光祿大夫，下曰銀青榮祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the top of the second positive rank, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Belt and Purple Ribbon; below, Grand Master of Glorious Happiness with Silver Belt and Blue Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the second positive rank is Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Belt and Purple Ribbon; below it, Grand Master of Glorious Happiness with Silver Belt and Blue Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 從二品上曰光祿大夫，下曰榮祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the top of the second secondary rank, Grand Master of the Imperial Household; below, Grand Master of Honor.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the second secondary rank is Grand Master of the Imperial Household; below it, Grand Master of Honor.

sentences.zh: 正三品上曰資德大夫，中曰資政大夫，下曰資善大夫。

translations.literal: At the top of the third positive rank, Grand Master of Assisting Virtue; in the middle, Grand Master of Assisting Governance; below, Grand Master of Assisting Goodness.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the third positive rank is Grand Master of Assisting Virtue; in the middle, Grand Master of Assisting Governance; at the bottom, Grand Master of Assisting Goodness.

sentences.zh: 從三品上曰正奉大夫，中曰通奉大夫，下曰中奉大夫。

translations.literal: At the top of the third secondary rank, Grand Master for Direct Audience; in the middle, Grand Master for Regular Audience; below, Grand Master for Attending Audience.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the third secondary rank is Grand Master for Direct Audience; in the middle, Grand Master for Regular Audience; at the bottom, Grand Master for Attending Audience.

sentences.zh: 正四品上曰正議大夫，中曰通議大夫，下曰嘉議大夫。

translations.literal: At the top of the fourth positive rank, Grand Master for Direct Discussion; in the middle, Grand Master for Regular Discussion; below, Grand Master for Commendable Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the fourth positive rank is Grand Master for Direct Discussion; in the middle, Grand Master for Regular Discussion; at the bottom, Grand Master for Commendable Discussion.

sentences.zh: 從四品上曰大中大夫，中曰中大夫，下曰少中大夫。

translations.literal: At the top of the fourth secondary rank, Grand Master of Palace Attendance; in the middle, Palace Attendant Grand Master; below, Junior Palace Attendant Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the fourth secondary rank is Grand Master of Palace Attendance; in the middle, Palace Attendant Grand Master; at the bottom, Junior Palace Attendant Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 正五品上曰中議大夫，中曰中憲大夫，下曰中順大夫。

translations.literal: At the top of the fifth positive rank, Grand Master for Central Discussion; in the middle, Grand Master for Central Rectification; below, Grand Master for Central Compliance.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the fifth positive rank is Grand Master for Central Discussion; in the middle, Grand Master for Central Rectification; at the bottom, Grand Master for Central Compliance.

sentences.zh: 從五品上曰朝請大夫，中曰朝散大夫，下曰朝列大夫。

translations.literal: At the top of the fifth secondary rank, Grand Master for Court Audience; in the middle, Grand Master for Dispersal at Court; below, Grand Master for Court Arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the fifth secondary rank is Grand Master for Court Audience; in the middle, Grand Master for Dispersal at Court; at the bottom, Grand Master for Court Arrangement.

sentences.zh: 舊日奉德大夫，天德二年更。

translations.literal: Formerly it was Grand Master of Virtuous Tribute; changed in Tiande year 2.
translations.idiomatic: It had formerly been Grand Master of Virtuous Tribute; the title was changed in Tiande year 2.

sentences.zh: 正六品上曰奉政大夫，下曰奉議大夫。

translations.literal: At the top of the sixth positive rank, Grand Master for Assisting Governance; below, Grand Master for Assisting Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the sixth positive rank is Grand Master for Assisting Governance; below it, Grand Master for Assisting Discussion.

sentences.zh: 從六品上曰奉直大夫，下曰奉訓大夫。

translations.literal: At the top of the sixth secondary rank, Grand Master for Direct Assistance; below, Grand Master for Assisting Instruction.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the sixth secondary rank is Grand Master for Direct Assistance; below it, Grand Master for Assisting Instruction.

sentences.zh: 正七品上曰承德郎，下曰承直郎。

translations.literal: At the top of the seventh positive rank, Gentleman for Honoring Virtue; below, Gentleman for Honoring Uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the seventh positive rank is Gentleman for Honoring Virtue; below it, Gentleman for Honoring Uprightness.

sentences.zh: 從七品上曰承務郎，下曰儒林郎。

translations.literal: At the top of the seventh secondary rank, Gentleman for Honoring Affairs; below, Gentleman of the Forest of Scholars.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the seventh secondary rank is Gentleman for Honoring Affairs; below it, Gentleman of the Forest of Scholars.

sentences.zh: 正八品上曰文林郎，下曰承事郎。

translations.literal: At the top of the eighth positive rank, Gentleman of the Forest of Letters; below, Gentleman for Honoring Service.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the eighth positive rank is Gentleman of the Forest of Letters; below it, Gentleman for Honoring Service.

sentences.zh: 從八品上曰征事郎，下曰從仕郎。

translations.literal: At the top of the eighth secondary rank, Gentleman for Attending Affairs; below, Gentleman for Following Service.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the eighth secondary rank is Gentleman for Attending Affairs; below it, Gentleman for Following Service.

sentences.zh: 正九品上曰登仕郎，下曰將仕郎。

translations.literal: At the top of the ninth positive rank, Gentleman for Entering Service; below, Gentleman for Awaiting Service.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the ninth positive rank is Gentleman for Entering Service; below it, Gentleman for Awaiting Service.

sentences.zh: 從九品上曰登仕佐郎，下曰將仕佐郎。

translations.literal: At the top of the ninth secondary rank, Assistant Gentleman for Entering Service; below, Assistant Gentleman for Awaiting Service.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the ninth secondary rank is Assistant Gentleman for Entering Service; below it, Assistant Gentleman for Awaiting Service.

sentences.zh: 此二階，大定十四年創增。

translations.literal: These two grades were newly added in Dading year 14.
translations.idiomatic: These two grades were first established in Dading year 14.

sentences.zh: 武散官，凡仕至從二品以上至從一品者，皆用文資。

translations.literal: Military scattered ranks: for all who serve from the second secondary rank upward through the first secondary rank, civil rank titles are all used.
translations.idiomatic: For military scattered ranks, anyone serving from the second secondary rank up through the first secondary rank uses civil rank titles.

sentences.zh: 自正三品以下，階與文資同：正三品上曰龍虎衛上將軍，中曰金吾衛上將軍，下曰驃騎衛上將軍。

translations.literal: From the third positive rank downward, the grades are the same as for civil ranks: at the top of the third positive rank, General-in-Chief of the Dragon-Tiger Guard; in the middle, General-in-Chief of the Golden Crow Guard; below, General-in-Chief of the Flying Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: From the third positive rank down, the grades match those of civil ranks: at the top of the third positive rank is General-in-Chief of the Dragon-Tiger Guard; in the middle, General-in-Chief of the Golden Crow Guard; at the bottom, General-in-Chief of the Flying Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 從三品上曰奉國上將軍，中曰輔國上將軍，下曰鎮國上將軍。

translations.literal: At the top of the third secondary rank, General-in-Chief for Serving the State; in the middle, General-in-Chief for Assisting the State; below, General-in-Chief for Pacifying the State.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the third secondary rank is General-in-Chief for Serving the State; in the middle, General-in-Chief for Assisting the State; at the bottom, General-in-Chief for Pacifying the State.

sentences.zh: 正四品上曰昭武大將軍，中曰昭毅大將軍，下曰昭勇大將軍。

translations.literal: At the top of the fourth positive rank, Grand General of Manifest Martiality; in the middle, Grand General of Manifest Resolution; below, Grand General of Manifest Courage.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the fourth positive rank is Grand General of Manifest Martiality; in the middle, Grand General of Manifest Resolution; at the bottom, Grand General of Manifest Courage.

sentences.zh: 從四品上曰安遠大將軍，中曰定遠大將軍，下曰懷遠大將軍。

translations.literal: At the top of the fourth secondary rank, Grand General for Pacifying the Distant; in the middle, Grand General for Settling the Distant; below, Grand General for Cherishing the Distant.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the fourth secondary rank is Grand General for Pacifying the Distant; in the middle, Grand General for Settling the Distant; at the bottom, Grand General for Cherishing the Distant.

sentences.zh: 正五品上曰廣威將軍，中曰宣威將軍，下曰明威將軍。

translations.literal: At the top of the fifth positive rank, General of Broad Authority; in the middle, General of Proclaimed Authority; below, General of Illustrious Authority.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the fifth positive rank is General of Broad Authority; in the middle, General of Proclaimed Authority; at the bottom, General of Illustrious Authority.

sentences.zh: 從五品上曰信武將軍，中曰顯武將軍，下曰宣武將軍。

translations.literal: At the top of the fifth secondary rank, General of Trustworthy Martiality; in the middle, General of Eminent Martiality; below, General of Proclaimed Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the fifth secondary rank is General of Trustworthy Martiality; in the middle, General of Eminent Martiality; at the bottom, General of Proclaimed Martiality.

sentences.zh: 正六品上曰武節將軍，下曰武德將軍。

translations.literal: At the top of the sixth positive rank, General of Martial Merit; below, General of Martial Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the sixth positive rank is General of Martial Merit; below it, General of Martial Virtue.

sentences.zh: 從六品上曰武義將軍，下曰武略將軍。

translations.literal: At the top of the sixth secondary rank, General of Martial Righteousness; below, General of Martial Strategy.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the sixth secondary rank is General of Martial Righteousness; below it, General of Martial Strategy.

sentences.zh: 正七品上曰承信校尉，下曰昭信校尉。

translations.literal: At the top of the seventh positive rank, Colonel for Upholding Trust; below, Colonel of Manifest Trust.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the seventh positive rank is Colonel for Upholding Trust; below it, Colonel of Manifest Trust.

sentences.zh: 從七品上曰忠武校尉，下曰忠顯校尉。

translations.literal: At the top of the seventh secondary rank, Loyal and Martial Colonel; below, Loyal and Eminent Colonel.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the seventh secondary rank is Loyal and Martial Colonel; below it, Loyal and Eminent Colonel.

sentences.zh: 正八品上曰忠勇校尉，下曰忠翊校尉。

translations.literal: At the top of the eighth positive rank, Loyal and Courageous Colonel; below, Loyal and Assisting Colonel.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the eighth positive rank is Loyal and Courageous Colonel; below it, Loyal and Assisting Colonel.

sentences.zh: 從八品上曰修武校尉，下曰敦武校尉。

translations.literal: At the top of the eighth secondary rank, Colonel for Cultivating Martiality; below, Colonel for Honest Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the eighth secondary rank is Colonel for Cultivating Martiality; below it, Colonel for Honest Martiality.

sentences.zh: 正九品上曰保義校尉，下曰進義校尉。

translations.literal: At the top of the ninth positive rank, Colonel for Upholding Righteousness; below, Colonel for Advancing Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the ninth positive rank is Colonel for Upholding Righteousness; below it, Colonel for Advancing Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 從九品上曰保義副尉，下曰進義副尉。

translations.literal: At the top of the ninth secondary rank, Assistant Colonel for Upholding Righteousness; below, Assistant Colonel for Advancing Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the ninth secondary rank is Assistant Colonel for Upholding Righteousness; below it, Assistant Colonel for Advancing Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 此二階，大定十四年創增。

translations.literal: These two grades were newly added in Dading year 14.
translations.idiomatic: These two grades were first established in Dading year 14.

sentences.zh: 封爵：正從一品曰郡王，曰國公。

translations.literal: Enfeoffment ranks: at the first positive and secondary ranks, Prince of a Commandery and State Duke.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffment ranks: at the first positive and secondary ranks are Prince of a Commandery and State Duke.

sentences.zh: 正從二品曰郡公。

translations.literal: At the second positive and secondary ranks, Commandery Duke.
translations.idiomatic: At the second positive and secondary ranks is Commandery Duke.

sentences.zh: 正從三品曰郡侯。

translations.literal: At the third positive and secondary ranks, Commandery Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: At the third positive and secondary ranks is Commandery Marquis.

sentences.zh: 正從四品曰郡伯。

translations.literal: At the fourth positive and secondary ranks, Commandery Earl.
translations.idiomatic: At the fourth positive and secondary ranks is Commandery Earl.

sentences.zh: 舊曰縣伯，承安二年更。

translations.literal: Formerly called County Earl; changed in Chengan year 2.
translations.idiomatic: It had formerly been called County Earl; the title was changed in Chengan year 2.

sentences.zh: 正五品曰縣子，從五品曰縣男。

translations.literal: At the fifth positive rank, County Viscount; at the fifth secondary rank, County Baron.
translations.idiomatic: At the fifth positive rank is County Viscount; at the fifth secondary rank, County Baron.

sentences.zh: 凡勳級：正二品曰上柱國，從二品曰柱國。

translations.literal: Merit grades in general: at the second positive rank, Upper Pillar of the State; at the second secondary rank, Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: Merit grades in general: at the second positive rank is Upper Pillar of the State; at the second secondary rank, Pillar of the State.

sentences.zh: 正三品曰上護軍，從三品曰護軍。

translations.literal: At the third positive rank, Upper Protector of the Army; at the third secondary rank, Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the third positive rank is Upper Protector of the Army; at the third secondary rank, Protector of the Army.

sentences.zh: 正四品曰上輕車都尉，從四品曰輕車都尉。

translations.literal: At the fourth positive rank, Upper Commandant of Light Chariots; at the fourth secondary rank, Commandant of Light Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: At the fourth positive rank is Upper Commandant of Light Chariots; at the fourth secondary rank, Commandant of Light Chariots.

sentences.zh: 正五品曰上騎都尉，從五品曰騎都尉。

translations.literal: At the fifth positive rank, Upper Commandant of Cavalry; at the fifth secondary rank, Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: At the fifth positive rank is Upper Commandant of Cavalry; at the fifth secondary rank, Commandant of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 正六品曰驍騎尉，從六品曰飛騎尉。

translations.literal: At the sixth positive rank, Captain of Valiant Cavalry; at the sixth secondary rank, Captain of Flying Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: At the sixth positive rank is Captain of Valiant Cavalry; at the sixth secondary rank, Captain of Flying Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 正七品曰雲騎尉，從七品曰武騎尉。

translations.literal: At the seventh positive rank, Captain of Cloud Cavalry; at the seventh secondary rank, Captain of Martial Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: At the seventh positive rank is Captain of Cloud Cavalry; at the seventh secondary rank, Captain of Martial Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 凡食邑：封王者萬戶，實封一千戶。

translations.literal: Stipendiary estates in general: for those enfeoffed as princes, ten thousand households nominally, one thousand households in actual fief.
translations.idiomatic: Stipendiary estates in general: princely enfeoffment carried ten thousand nominal households and one thousand actual fief households.

sentences.zh: 郡王五千戶，實封五百戶。

translations.literal: Princes of a Commandery, five thousand households; actual fief, five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Princes of a Commandery received five thousand nominal households and five hundred actual fief households.

sentences.zh: 國公三千戶，實封三百戶。

translations.literal: State Dukes, three thousand households; actual fief, three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: State Dukes received three thousand nominal households and three hundred actual fief households.

sentences.zh: 郡公二千戶，實封二百戶。

translations.literal: Commandery Dukes, two thousand households; actual fief, two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery Dukes received two thousand nominal households and two hundred actual fief households.

sentences.zh: 郡侯一千戶，實封一百戶。

translations.literal: Commandery Marquises, one thousand households; actual fief, one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery Marquises received one thousand nominal households and one hundred actual fief households.

sentences.zh: 郡伯七百戶，縣子五百戶，縣男三百戶，皆無實封。

translations.literal: Commandery Earls, seven hundred households; County Viscounts, five hundred households; County Barons, three hundred households—all without actual fief.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery Earls received seven hundred households, County Viscounts five hundred, and County Barons three hundred; none of these carried an actual fief.

sentences.zh: 自天眷定制，凡食邑，同散官入銜。

translations.literal: Since the Tianjuan institutional reform, all stipendiary estates enter the title together with scattered ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Tianjuan institutional reform, stipendiary estates have been entered into the title together with scattered ranks.

sentences.zh: 司天翰林官，舊制自從七品而下止五階，至天眷定制，司天自從四品而下，立為十五階：從四品上曰欽象大夫，中曰正儀大夫，下曰欽授大夫。

translations.literal: Directorate of Astronomy officials: under the old system from the seventh secondary rank downward there were only five grades; by the Tianjuan institutional reform, the Directorate of Astronomy from the fourth secondary rank downward was established in fifteen grades: at the top of the fourth secondary rank, Grand Master of Revering the Cosmos; in the middle, Grand Master of Correct Ritual; below, Grand Master of Revering Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Directorate of Astronomy officials: under the old system there were only five grades from the seventh secondary rank down; under the Tianjuan institutional reform the directorate was given fifteen grades from the fourth secondary rank down: at the top of the fourth secondary rank is Grand Master of Revering the Cosmos; in the middle, Grand Master of Correct Ritual; at the bottom, Grand Master of Revering Transmission.

sentences.zh: 正五品上曰靈憲大夫，中曰明時大夫，下曰頒朔大夫。

translations.literal: At the top of the fifth positive rank, Grand Master of Spiritual Statutes; in the middle, Grand Master of Clarifying the Seasons; below, Grand Master of Proclaiming the New Moon.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the fifth positive rank is Grand Master of Spiritual Statutes; in the middle, Grand Master of Clarifying the Seasons; at the bottom, Grand Master of Proclaiming the New Moon.

sentences.zh: 從五品上曰雲紀大夫，中曰協紀大夫，下曰保章大夫。

translations.literal: At the top of the fifth secondary rank, Grand Master of Cloud Records; in the middle, Grand Master of Harmonizing Records; below, Grand Master of Preserving the Observations.
translations.idiomatic: At the top of the fifth secondary rank is Grand Master of Cloud Records; in the middle, Grand Master of Harmonizing Records; at the bottom, Grand Master of Preserving the Observations.

sentences.zh: 凡內外官之政績，所曆之資考，更代之期，去就之故，秩滿皆備陳于解由，吏部據以定能否。

translations.literal: For all inner and outer officials, their administrative achievements, seniority reviews through posts held, schedules for replacement, and reasons for departure or appointment—when a term expires all are fully set forth in the certificate of release, and the Ministry of Personnel relies on these to determine fitness for office.
translations.idiomatic: For all inner and outer officials, administrative achievements, seniority reviews through posts held, replacement schedules, and reasons for departure or appointment are fully recorded in the certificate of release when a term expires; the Ministry of Personnel uses these records to judge fitness for office.

sentences.zh: 又撮解由之要，于銓擬時讀之，謂之銓頭。

translations.literal: Moreover, the essential points from the certificate of release are excerpted and read at the time of selection and nomination—this is called the selection headnote.
translations.idiomatic: The essential points from each certificate are excerpted and read at the time of selection and nomination; this summary is called the selection headnote.

sentences.zh: 又會歷任銓頭，而書于行止簿。

translations.literal: Selection headnotes from successive appointments are compiled and entered in the Conduct Register.
translations.idiomatic: Selection headnotes from successive appointments are compiled and entered in the Conduct Register.

sentences.zh: 行止簿者，以姓為類，而書各人平日所曆之資考功過者也。

translations.literal: The Conduct Register arranges entries by surname and records each person's accumulated seniority reviews, merits, and faults from ordinary service.
translations.idiomatic: The Conduct Register arranges entries by surname and records each official's accumulated seniority reviews, merits, and faults from ordinary service.

sentences.zh: 又為簿，列百司官名，有所更代，則以小黃綾書更代之期，及所以去就之故，而制其銓擬之要領焉。

translations.literal: Another register lists the official names of all bureaus; when replacements occur, the schedule for rotation and the reasons for departure or appointment are written on small yellow silk slips, thereby governing the essentials of selection and nomination.
translations.idiomatic: Another register lists the official names of all bureaus; when replacements occur, the rotation schedule and the reasons for departure or appointment are written on small yellow silk slips, thereby governing the essentials of selection and nomination.

sentences.zh: 凡縣令，則省除、部除者通書而各疏之。

translations.literal: For county magistrates, appointments from provincial commission and ministerial commission are entered together in the report and each is itemized separately.
translations.idiomatic: For county magistrates, appointments made by provincial commission and by ministerial commission are recorded together in the evaluation report, with each appointment itemized separately.

sentences.zh: 泰和四年，定考課法，准唐令，作四善、十七最之制。

translations.literal: In Taihe year 4, the performance-evaluation law was established; following Tang statutes, a system of Four Virtues and Seventeen Excellences was instituted.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year 4 the performance-evaluation law was established; following Tang regulations, the Jin adopted the system of Four Virtues and Seventeen Excellences.

sentences.zh: 四善之一曰德義有聞，二曰清慎明著，三曰公平可稱，四曰勤恪匪懈。

translations.literal: Of the Four Virtues, the first is that virtue and righteousness are renowned; the second, that purity and prudence are manifest; the third, that fairness is commendable; the fourth, that diligence and earnestness are never slackened.
translations.idiomatic: The Four Virtues were these: first, that one's virtue and righteousness are widely known; second, that one's purity and prudence are clearly evident; third, that one's fairness is praiseworthy; fourth, that one's diligence and earnestness never flag.

sentences.zh: 十七最之一曰禮樂興行，肅清所部，為政教之最。

translations.literal: Of the Seventeen Excellences, the first is that rites and music flourish and the district is kept in order, ranking as the excellence in governance and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The first of the Seventeen Excellences was that rites and music flourish and the jurisdiction is kept in good order—the highest mark in governance and instruction.

sentences.zh: 二曰賦役均平，田野加辟，為牧民之最。

translations.literal: The second is that tax and corvée levies are even and the fields are further opened to cultivation, ranking as the excellence in nurturing the people.
translations.idiomatic: The second was even tax and corvée levies and further opening of the fields—the highest mark in caring for the people.

sentences.zh: 三曰決斷不滯，與奪當理，為判事之最。

translations.literal: The third is that judgments are not delayed and grants and denials accord with reason, ranking as the excellence in adjudicating cases.
translations.idiomatic: The third was prompt adjudication and grants and denials in accord with reason—the highest mark in deciding cases.

sentences.zh: 四曰鈐束吏卒，奸盜不滋，為嚴明之最。

translations.literal: The fourth is that clerks and guards are kept in discipline and theft and brigandage do not proliferate, ranking as the excellence in strictness and clarity.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth was strict control of clerks and guards and the suppression of theft and brigandage—the highest mark in strict and clear administration.

sentences.zh: 五曰案簿分明，評擬均當，為檢校之最。

translations.literal: The fifth is that case records are clear and evaluations and nominations are fitting, ranking as the excellence in auditing and verification.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth was clear case records and fair evaluations and nominations—the highest mark in auditing and verification.

sentences.zh: 以上皆謂縣令、丞簿、警巡使副、錄事、司候、判官也。

translations.literal: The above all refer to county magistrates, assistant magistrates and registrars, chief and deputy police patrol commissioners, record clerks, gate inspectors, and judicial aides.
translations.idiomatic: The above all applied to county magistrates, assistant magistrates and registrars, chief and deputy police patrol commissioners, record clerks, gate inspectors, and judicial aides.

sentences.zh: 六曰詳斷合宜，咨執當理，為幕職之最。

translations.literal: The sixth is that detailed adjudication is appropriate and consultation and execution accord with reason, ranking as the excellence for staff officers.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth was appropriate detailed adjudication and consultation and execution in accord with reason—the highest mark for staff officers.

sentences.zh: 七曰盜賊消弭，使人安靜，為巡捕之最。

translations.literal: The seventh is that bandits and thieves are eliminated and the people live in peace, ranking as the excellence in patrol and arrest.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh was the elimination of bandits and thieves and the peace of the people—the highest mark in patrol and arrest.

sentences.zh: 八曰明于出納，物無損失，為倉庫之最。

translations.literal: The eighth is mastery of receipts and disbursements with no loss of goods, ranking as the excellence in granaries and stores.
translations.idiomatic: The eighth was mastery of receipts and disbursements with no loss of goods—the highest mark in granaries and storehouses.

sentences.zh: 九曰訓導有方，生徒充業，為學官之最。

translations.literal: The ninth is effective instruction and students fully completing their studies, ranking as the excellence for educational officers.
translations.idiomatic: The ninth was effective instruction and students fully completing their studies—the highest mark for educational officers.

sentences.zh: 十曰檢察有方，行旅無滯，為關津之最。

translations.literal: The tenth is thorough inspection so that travelers are not delayed, ranking as the excellence at passes and ferries.
translations.idiomatic: The tenth was thorough inspection so that travelers were not delayed—the highest mark at passes and ferries.

sentences.zh: 十一曰堤防堅固，備禦無虞，為河防之最。

translations.literal: The eleventh is that dikes are solid and defenses prepared without cause for concern, ranking as the excellence in river flood control.
translations.idiomatic: The eleventh was solid dikes and prepared defenses without cause for alarm—the highest mark in river flood control.

sentences.zh: 十二曰出納明敏，數無濫失，為監督之最。

translations.literal: The twelfth is clear and efficient handling of receipts and disbursements with no excess or loss in the accounts, ranking as the excellence in supervision.
translations.idiomatic: The twelfth was clear and efficient receipts and disbursements with no excess or loss in the accounts—the highest mark in supervisory posts.

sentences.zh: 十三曰謹察禁囚，輕重無怨，為獄官之最。

translations.literal: The thirteenth is careful oversight of prisoners with no grievances regarding severity of punishment, ranking as the excellence for prison officials.
translations.idiomatic: The thirteenth was careful oversight of prisoners with no grievances over the severity of punishment—the highest mark for prison officials.

sentences.zh: 十四曰物價得實，奸濫不行，為市司之最，謂市令也。

translations.literal: The fourteenth is that commodity prices are accurate and fraud and adulteration do not occur, ranking as the excellence for market officials—meaning market commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: The fourteenth was accurate commodity prices and the suppression of fraud and adulteration—the highest mark for market officials, that is, market commissioners.

sentences.zh: 十五曰戎器完肅，捍守有方，為邊防之最，謂正副部隊將、鎮防官也。

translations.literal: The fifteenth is that military equipment is complete and defense is well managed, ranking as the excellence in frontier defense—meaning primary and deputy unit commanders and garrison officers.
translations.idiomatic: The fifteenth was complete military equipment and effective defense—the highest mark in frontier defense, meaning primary and deputy unit commanders and garrison officers.

sentences.zh: 十六曰議獄得情，處斷公平，為法官之最。

translations.literal: The sixteenth is that legal deliberation grasps the facts and adjudication is fair, ranking as the excellence for judicial officers.
translations.idiomatic: The sixteenth was legal deliberation that grasped the facts and fair adjudication—the highest mark for judicial officers.

sentences.zh: 十七曰差役均平，盜賊止息，為軍職之最，謂都軍、軍轄也。

translations.literal: The seventeenth is that corvée assignments are even and bandits and thieves cease, ranking as the excellence for military posts—meaning army commanders and military administrators.
translations.idiomatic: The seventeenth was even corvée assignment and the cessation of banditry—the highest mark for military posts, meaning army commanders and military administrators.

sentences.zh: 凡縣令以下，三最以上有四善或三善者為上，升一等，三最以上有二善者為中，減兩資歷，三最以上有一善為下，減一資歷。

translations.literal: For county magistrates and below, those with three or more excellences and four or three virtues rank as superior and advance one grade; those with three or more excellences and two virtues rank as middle and have two years of seniority deducted; those with three or more excellences and one virtue rank as inferior and have one year of seniority deducted.
translations.idiomatic: For county magistrates and below, an official with three or more excellences and four or three virtues was rated superior and advanced one grade; three excellences and two virtues rated middle, with two years of seniority deducted; three excellences and one virtue rated inferior, with one year of seniority deducted.

sentences.zh: 節度判官、防禦判官、軍判以下，一最而有四善或三善為上，減一資歷，一最而有二善為中，升為榜首，一最而有一善為下，升本等首。

translations.literal: For military commissioners' judicial aides, defense commissioners' judicial aides, and army judges and below, one excellence with four or three virtues ranks as superior and one year of seniority is deducted; one excellence with two virtues ranks as middle and advances to head of the nomination list; one excellence with one virtue ranks as inferior and advances to head of that grade.
translations.idiomatic: For judicial aides to military commissioners and defense commissioners, and for army judges and below, one excellence with four or three virtues rated superior, with one year of seniority deducted; one excellence with two virtues rated middle and placed at the head of the nomination list; one excellence with one virtue rated inferior and placed at the head of that grade.

sentences.zh: 又以明昌四年所定，軍民俱稱為廉能者是為廉能官之制，參於其間而定其甄擢焉。

translations.literal: Further, according to what was established in Mingchang year 4, officials whom both military and civilians alike praised as upright and capable constituted the system of upright-and-capable officials, and this was incorporated into the evaluation to determine promotion.
translations.idiomatic: In addition, the standard established in Mingchang year 4 identified officials whom both soldiers and civilians praised as upright and capable—the system of upright-and-capable officials—and this criterion was woven into evaluations to determine promotion.

sentences.zh: 宣宗興定元年，行辟舉縣令法，以六事考之，一曰田野辟，二曰戶口增，三曰賦役平，四曰盜賊息，五曰軍民和，六曰詞訟簡。

translations.literal: In Xingding year 1 of Emperor Xuanzong, the method of recommending county magistrates was implemented, evaluating them on six matters: first, land reclamation; second, population increase; third, even tax and corvée levies; fourth, suppression of banditry; fifth, harmony between military and civilians; sixth, reduction of litigation.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingding year 1 Emperor Xuanzong instituted a system of recommending county magistrates, evaluated on six criteria: land reclamation, population growth, even tax and corvée levies, suppressed banditry, harmony between military and civilians, and reduced litigation.

sentences.zh: 六事俱備為上等，升職一等。

translations.literal: Fulfillment of all six matters ranked as superior, with advancement of one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Meeting all six criteria rated superior and earned advancement of one grade.

sentences.zh: 兼四事者為中等，減二資歷。

translations.literal: Meeting four matters ranked as middle, with two years of seniority deducted.
translations.idiomatic: Meeting four criteria rated middle, with two years of seniority deducted.

sentences.zh: 其次為下等，減一資歷。

translations.literal: The next rank was inferior, with one year of seniority deducted.
translations.idiomatic: Below that rated inferior, with one year of seniority deducted.

sentences.zh: 否則為不稱職，罷而降之。

translations.literal: Otherwise the official was deemed unfit for office and dismissed or demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the magistrate was judged unfit for office and dismissed or demoted.

sentences.zh: 平常者依本格。

translations.literal: Average performers followed the standard regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Average performers were handled according to the standard regulations.

sentences.zh: 凡封王：大國號二十，曰：恆舊為遼，明昌二年以漢、遼、唐、宋、梁、秦、殷、楚之類，皆昔有天下者之號，不宜封臣下，遂皆改之、邵舊為梁、汴舊為宋、鎬舊為秦、並舊為晉、益舊為漢、彭舊為齊、趙、越、譙舊為殷、郢舊為楚、魯、冀、豫、絳舊為唐、袞、鄂舊為吳、夔舊為蜀、宛舊為陳、曹。

translations.literal: For enfeoffment as prince: there were twenty great-state titles, namely: Heng, formerly Liao—in Mingchang year 2 titles such as Han, Liao, Tang, Song, Liang, Qin, Yin, and Chu, all names of former dynasties that had possessed the realm, were deemed unsuitable for enfeoffing subjects and were all changed; Shao, formerly Liang; Bian, formerly Song; Hao, formerly Qin; Bing, formerly Jin; Yi, formerly Han; Peng, formerly Qi; Zhao; Yue; Qiao, formerly Yin; Ying, formerly Chu; Lu; Ji; Yu; Jiang, formerly Tang; Gun; E, formerly Wu; Kui, formerly Shu; Wan, formerly Chen; and Cao.
translations.idiomatic: For enfeoffment as prince there were twenty great-state titles: Heng, formerly Liao—in Mingchang year 2 names such as Han, Liao, Tang, Song, Liang, Qin, Yin, and Chu, all titles of former dynasties that had once ruled the realm, were judged unsuitable for enfeoffing subjects and were all changed; Shao, formerly Liang; Bian, formerly Song; Hao, formerly Qin; Bing, formerly Jin; Yi, formerly Han; Peng, formerly Qi; Zhao; Yue; Qiao, formerly Yin; Ying, formerly Chu; Lu; Ji; Yu; Jiang, formerly Tang; Gun; E, formerly Wu; Kui, formerly Shu; Wan, formerly Chen; and Cao.

sentences.zh: 次國三十，曰：涇舊為隋、鄭、衛、韓、潞、豳、沈、岐、代、澤、徐、滕、薛、紀、升舊為原、邢、翼、豐、畢、鄧、鄆、霍、蔡、瀛按金格，葛當在此、沂、荊、榮、英、壽、溫。

translations.literal: Thirty secondary states, namely: Jing, formerly Sui; Zheng; Wei; Han; Lu; Bin; Shen; Qi; Dai; Ze; Xu; Teng; Xue; Ji; Sheng, formerly Yuan; Xing; Yi; Feng; Bi; Deng; Yun; Huo; Cai; Ying—according to Jin regulations, Ge ought to be here; Yi; Jing; Rong; Ying; Shou; and Wen.
translations.idiomatic: There were thirty secondary states: Jing, formerly Sui; Zheng; Wei; Han; Lu; Bin; Shen; Qi; Dai; Ze; Xu; Teng; Xue; Ji; Sheng, formerly Yuan; Xing; Yi; Feng; Bi; Deng; Yun; Huo; Cai; Ying—according to Jin regulations, Ge ought to appear here; Yi; Jing; Rong; Ying; Shou; and Wen.

sentences.zh: 小國三十：濮、遂舊曰濟、道、定、景後改為鄒、申、崇、宿、息、莒、鄴、郜、舒、淄、郕、萊舊為宗，以避諱改、鄖、郯、杞、向、管舊曰郇，興定元年改、密、胙、任、戴、鞏、蔣《士民須知》雲舊為葛、蕭、莘、芮。

translations.literal: Thirty minor states: Pu; Sui, formerly called Ji; Dao; Ding; Jing, later changed to Zou; Shen; Chong; Su; Xi; Ju; Ye; Gao; Shu; Zi; Cheng; Lai, formerly Zong, changed to avoid taboo; Yun; Tan; Qi; Xiang; Guan, formerly called Xun, changed in Xingding year 1; Mi; Zuo; Ren; Dai; Gong; Jiang—Essentials for Officials and People states that Jiang was formerly Ge; Xiao; Shen; and Rui.
translations.idiomatic: There were thirty minor states: Pu; Sui, formerly Ji; Dao; Ding; Jing, later changed to Zou; Shen; Chong; Su; Xi; Ju; Ye; Gao; Shu; Zi; Cheng; Lai, formerly Zong, changed to avoid taboo; Yun; Tan; Qi; Xiang; Guan, formerly Xun, changed in Xingding year 1; Mi; Zuo; Ren; Dai; Gong; Jiang—Essentials for Officials and People states that Jiang was formerly Ge; Xiao; Shen; and Rui.

sentences.zh: 封王之郡號十：金源、廣平、平原、南陽、常山、太原、平陽、東平、安定、延安。

translations.literal: Ten commandery titles for princely enfeoffment: Jinyuan, Guangping, Pingyuan, Nanyang, Changshan, Taiyuan, Pingyang, Dongping, Anding, and Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ten commandery titles were used for princely enfeoffment: Jinyuan, Guangping, Pingyuan, Nanyang, Changshan, Taiyuan, Pingyang, Dongping, Anding, and Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 封公主之縣號三十：樂安、清平、蓬萊、榮安、棲霞、壽光、靈仙、壽陽、鐘秀、惠和、永甯、慶雲、靜樂、福山、隆平、德平、文安、福昌、順安、樂壽、靜安、靈壽、大寧、聞喜、秀容、宜芳、真寧、嘉祥、金鄉、華原。

translations.literal: Thirty county titles for enfeoffment of princesses: Le'an, Qingping, Penglai, Rong'an, Qixia, Shouguang, Lingxian, Shouyang, Zhongxiu, Huihe, Yongning, Qingyun, Jingyue, Fushan, Longping, Deping, Wen'an, Fuchang, Shun'an, Leshou, Jing'an, Lingshou, Daning, Wenxi, Xiurong, Yifang, Zhenning, Jiaxiang, Jinxiang, and Huayuan.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty county titles were used for enfeoffment of princesses: Le'an, Qingping, Penglai, Rong'an, Qixia, Shouguang, Lingxian, Shouyang, Zhongxiu, Huihe, Yongning, Qingyun, Jingyue, Fushan, Longping, Deping, Wen'an, Fuchang, Shun'an, Leshou, Jing'an, Lingshou, Daning, Wenxi, Xiurong, Yifang, Zhenning, Jiaxiang, Jinxiang, and Huayuan.

sentences.zh: 凡白號之姓，完顏、溫蒂罕、夾谷、陀滿、僕散、術虎、移剌荅、斡勒、斡准、把、阿不罕、卓魯、回特、黑罕、會蘭、沈谷、塞蒲裏、吾古孫、石敦、卓陀、阿廝准、匹獨思、潘術古、諳石剌、石古苦、綴罕、光吉剌，皆封金源郡。

translations.literal: For white-banner clans, the surnames Wanyan, Wentehan, Jiagu, Tuoman, Pusan, Shuhu, Yilida, Wole, Wozhun, Ba, Abuhan, Zhuolu, Huite, Heihan, Huilan, Shengugu, Saipuli, Wugusun, Shidun, Zhuotuo, Asizhun, Pidusi, Panshugu, Anshila, Shiguku, Chuihan, and Guangjila were all enfeoffed as Jinyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For white-banner clans, the surnames Wanyan, Wentehan, Jiagu, Tuoman, Pusan, Shuhu, Yilida, Wole, Wozhun, Ba, Abuhan, Zhuolu, Huite, Heihan, Huilan, Shengugu, Saipuli, Wugusun, Shidun, Zhuotuo, Asizhun, Pidusi, Panshugu, Anshila, Shiguku, Chuihan, and Guangjila were all enfeoffed as Jinyuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 斐滿、徒單、溫敦、兀林荅、阿典、紇石烈、納闌、孛術魯、阿勒根、納合、石盞、蒲鮮、古裏甲、阿迭、聶摸欒、抹拈、納坦、兀撒惹、阿鮮、把古、溫古孫、耨碗、撒合烈、吾塞、和速嘉、能偃、阿裏班、兀裏坦、聶散、蒲速烈，皆封廣平郡。

translations.literal: The surnames Feiman, Tudan, Wendun, Wulinda, Adian, Heshilie, Nalan, Shushulu, Aleigen, Nahe, Shizhan, Puxian, Gulijia, Adie, Niemoquan, Monian, Nata, Wusare, Axian, Bagu, Wengusun, Nouwan, Sahelie, Wusai, Hesujia, Nengyan, Aliban, Wulitan, Niesan, and Pusulie were all enfeoffed as Guangping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The surnames Feiman, Tudan, Wendun, Wulinda, Adian, Heshilie, Nalan, Shushulu, Aleigen, Nahe, Shizhan, Puxian, Gulijia, Adie, Niemoquan, Monian, Nata, Wusare, Axian, Bagu, Wengusun, Nouwan, Sahelie, Wusai, Hesujia, Nengyan, Aliban, Wulitan, Niesan, and Pusulie were all enfeoffed as Guangping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 吾古論、兀顏、女奚烈、獨吉、黃摑、顏盞、蒲古裏，必蘭、斡雷、獨鼎、尼厖窟窟亦作古、拓特、盍散、撒荅牙、阿速、撒剗、准土穀、納謀魯、業速布、安煦烈、愛申、拿可、貴益昆、溫撒、梭罕、霍域，皆封隴西郡。

translations.literal: The surnames Wugulun, Wuyan, Nvxilie, Duji, Huangqin, Yanzhan, Puguli, Bilan, Wolei, Duding, Nimongkuku—also written Gu, Tuote, Hesana, Sadaya, Asu, Sacha, Zhuntugu, Namolu, Yesubu, Anxulie, Aishen, Nake, Guiyikun, Wensa, Suohan, and Huoyu were all enfeoffed as Longxi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The surnames Wugulun, Wuyan, Nvxilie, Duji, Huangqin, Yanzhan, Puguli, Bilan, Wolei, Duding, Nimongkuku—also written Gu—Tuote, Hesana, Sadaya, Asu, Sacha, Zhuntugu, Namolu, Yesubu, Anxulie, Aishen, Nake, Guiyikun, Wensa, Suohan, and Huoyu were all enfeoffed as Longxi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 黑號之姓，唐括舊書作同古、蒲察、術甲、蒙古、蒲速、粘割、奧屯、斜卯、准葛、諳蠻、獨虎、術魯、磨輦、益輦、帖暖、蘇孛輦，皆封彭城郡。

translations.literal: For black-banner clans, the surnames Tangguo—old texts write Tonggu—Pucha, Shujia, Menggu, Pusu, Nianqe, Aotun, Xiema, Zhunge, Anman, Duhu, Shulu, Monian, Yinian, Tienuan, and Subelinian were all enfeoffed as Pengcheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For black-banner clans, the surnames Tangguo—old texts write Tonggu—Pucha, Shujia, Menggu, Pusu, Nianqe, Aotun, Xiema, Zhunge, Anman, Duhu, Shulu, Monian, Yinian, Tienuan, and Subelinian were all enfeoffed as Pengcheng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 親王母妻，封一字王者舊封王妃，為正從一品。

translations.literal: The mother and wife of a prince enfeoffed with a single-character title—if previously enfeoffed as prince's consort—were ranked primary or secondary first grade.
translations.idiomatic: The mother and wife of a prince enfeoffed with a single-character title, if previously enfeoffed as prince's consort, held the rank of primary or secondary first grade.

sentences.zh: 次室封王夫人。

translations.literal: Concubines were enfeoffed as Lady of the Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: Concubines received the title Lady of the Prince's Household.

sentences.zh: 承安二年，敕王妃止封王夫人，次室封孺人。

translations.literal: In Chengan year 2, an edict stipulated that prince's consorts were enfeoffed only as Lady of the Prince's Household, and concubines as Lady.
translations.idiomatic: In Chengan year 2 an edict ruled that a prince's consort would receive only the title Lady of the Prince's Household, and a concubine the title Lady.

sentences.zh: 郡王母妻封郡王夫人，國公母妻封國公夫人，郡公母妻封郡公夫人，郡侯母妻封郡君承安二年更為郡侯夫人，四品文散少中大夫、武散懷遠大將軍以上母妻封縣君承安二年為郡君，五品文散朝列大夫、武散宣武將軍以上母妻封鄉君承安二年為縣君。

translations.literal: The mother and wife of a commandery prince were enfeoffed as Lady of the Commandery Prince; of a state duke, as Lady of the State Duke; of a commandery duke, as Lady of the Commandery Duke; of a commandery marquis, as Commandery Lady—in Chengan year 2 changed to Lady of the Commandery Marquis; the mother and wife of civil scattered officials from Junior Attendant-in-Regular-Session and above and military scattered officials from General of Far-Reaching Merit and above were enfeoffed as County Lady—in Chengan year 2 as Commandery Lady; the mother and wife of civil scattered officials from Attendant-in-Regular-Session and military scattered officials from General of Martial Valor and above were enfeoffed as Township Lady—in Chengan year 2 as County Lady.
translations.idiomatic: The mother and wife of a commandery prince received the title Lady of the Commandery Prince; of a state duke, Lady of the State Duke; of a commandery duke, Lady of the Commandery Duke; of a commandery marquis, Commandery Lady—in Chengan year 2 changed to Lady of the Commandery Marquis. The mother and wife of civil scattered officials from Junior Attendant-in-Regular-Session upward and military scattered officials from General of Far-Reaching Merit upward received County Lady—in Chengan year 2, Commandery Lady. The mother and wife of civil scattered officials from Attendant-in-Regular-Session upward and military scattered officials from General of Martial Valor upward received Township Lady—in Chengan year 2, County Lady.

sentences.zh: 皇統五年，以古官曰「牧」、曰「長」，各有總名，今庶官不分類為名，于文移不便。

translations.literal: In Huangtong year 5, because ancient offices were called "prefect" or "chief" and each had an umbrella designation, whereas miscellaneous offices now lacked categorical names, this made documentation inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong year 5 it was observed that ancient offices were called "prefect" or "chief" and each category had a general designation, whereas miscellaneous offices now lacked such categorical names, making official correspondence inconvenient.

sentences.zh: 遂定京府尹牧、留守、知州、縣令、詳穩、群牧為「長官」，同知、簽院、副使、少尹、通判、丞曰「佐貳官」，判官、推官、掌書記、主簿、縣尉為「幕職官」，兵馬司及它司軍者曰「軍職官」，警巡、市令、錄事、司候、諸參軍、知律、勘事、勘判為「厘務官」，應管倉庫院務者曰「監當官」監當官出大定制，知事孔目以下行文書者為「吏」。

translations.literal: Therefore designations were fixed: capital prefects, defense commissioners, prefects, county magistrates, xiangwen, and herd commissioners were called "chief officials"; vice commissioners, commissioners with signing authority, deputy commissioners, junior prefects, military-civilian controllers, and assistants were called "secondary officials"; judicial aides, investigating officers, secretaries, registrars, and county assistant magistrates were called "staff officers"; military affairs bureaus and other military commissions were called "military-post officials"; police patrol officers, market commissioners, record clerks, gate inspectors, administrative aides, law commissioners, investigating officers, and investigative judges were called "regulatory affairs officials"; those managing granaries, storehouses, and revenue offices were called "supervisory officials"—supervisory officials come from the Great Ordinances; clerks from chief clerks downward who draft documents were called "clerical staff."
translations.idiomatic: Designations were therefore fixed as follows: capital prefects, defense commissioners, prefects, county magistrates, xiangwen, and herd commissioners were called "chief officials"; vice commissioners, commissioners with signing authority, deputy commissioners, junior prefects, military-civilian controllers, and assistants were called "secondary officials"; judicial aides, investigating officers, secretaries, registrars, and county assistant magistrates were called "staff officers"; military affairs bureaus and other military commissions were called "military-post officials"; police patrol officers, market commissioners, record clerks, gate inspectors, administrative aides, law commissioners, investigating officers, and investigative judges were called "regulatory affairs officials"; those managing granaries, storehouses, and revenue offices were called "supervisory officials"—a term drawn from the Great Ordinances; clerks from chief clerks downward who drafted documents were called "clerical staff."

sentences.zh: 凡除拜，尚書令、左右丞相以下，品不同者，則帶「守」字。

translations.literal: For appointments, from the Director of the Secretariat and the Left and Right Chancellors downward, when rank differed the designation "acting" was added.
translations.idiomatic: In appointments, from the Director of the Secretariat and the Left and Right Chancellors downward, when an official's rank differed from the post, the designation "acting" was added.

sentences.zh: 左右丞則帶「行守」字。

translations.literal: The Left and Right Vice Chancellors added the designation "provisional acting."
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Vice Chancellors added the designation "provisional acting."

sentences.zh: 凡台官、禦史、部官、京尹、少尹、守令、丞、簿、尉、錄事、諸卿少至協律、評事、諫官、國子監學官、諸監至丞郎、符寶郎、東宮詹事、率府、僕正副、令丞、王府官，散官高於職事者帶「行」字，職事高於散官一品者帶「守」字、二品者帶「試」字，品同者皆否。

translations.literal: For censorate officials, investigating censors, ministry officials, capital prefects, junior prefects, magistrates, assistants, registrars, assistant magistrates, record clerks, assistant ministers of the Nine Ministers through harmonizing pitch officers, evaluating officers, remonstrance officials, Directorate of Education officials, supervisory offices through assistant directors, talisman officials, Eastern Palace officials, rate palaces, chief and deputy stewards, commandery officials, and prince's household officials: when scattered rank exceeded substantive rank the designation "acting" was added; when substantive rank exceeded scattered rank by one grade the designation "acting appointment" was added, by two grades "provisional"; when ranks matched, none was added.
translations.idiomatic: For censorate officials, investigating censors, ministry officials, capital prefects, junior prefects, magistrates, assistants, registrars, assistant magistrates, record clerks, assistant ministers of the Nine Ministers through harmonizing pitch officers, evaluating officers, remonstrance officials, Directorate of Education officials, supervisory offices through assistant directors, talisman officials, Eastern Palace officials, rate palaces, chief and deputy stewards, commandery officials, and prince's household officials: when scattered rank exceeded substantive rank, "acting" was added; when substantive rank exceeded scattered rank by one grade, "acting appointment" was added, and by two grades, "provisional"; when ranks matched, no designation was added.

sentences.zh: 猛安、謀克、翰林待制、修撰、判、推、勘事官、都事、典事、知事、內承奉、押班、通事舍人、通進、編修、勾當、頓舍、部役、廂官、受給管勾、巡河官、直省直院長副、諸檢法、知法、司正、教授、司獄、司候、東宮諭德、贊善、掌寶、典儀以下，王府文學、記事參軍，並帶「充」字。

translations.literal: Meng'an, mouke, Hanlin Academicians Awaiting Orders, compilers, judges, investigating officers, clerks of the chief office, recorders, inner attendants, duty officers, memorial-herald clerks, memorial transmitters, compilers, duty officers, supply officers, section officers, supply-account clerks, river-patrol officers, bureau chiefs and deputies, law inspectors, law commissioners, court masters, instructors, prison officers, gate inspectors, Eastern Palace instructors and aides, seal custodians, ceremonial officers and below, plus prince's household literary instructors and recording aides—all added the designation "commissioned."
translations.idiomatic: Meng'an, mouke, Hanlin Academicians Awaiting Orders, compilers, judges, investigating officers, clerks of the chief office, recorders, inner attendants, duty officers, memorial-herald clerks, memorial transmitters, compilers, duty officers, supply officers, section officers, supply-account clerks, river-patrol officers, bureau chiefs and deputies, law inspectors, law commissioners, court masters, instructors, prison officers, gate inspectors, Eastern Palace instructors and aides, seal custodians, ceremonial officers and below, and prince's household literary instructors and recording aides—all added the designation "commissioned."

sentences.zh: 樞密、宣徽、勸農、諸軍都指揮、統軍、轉運使、招討、提刑、節度、群牧、防禦、客省、引進、四方館、閣門、太醫、教坊、鷹坊、警巡、巡檢、諸司局倉庫務使副，皆帶「充」字及「知某事」。

translations.literal: The Privy Council, Palace Service, Agricultural Promotion, army commanders, army commissioners, transport commissioners, punitive commissioners, judicial commissioners, military commissioners, herd commissioners, defense commissioners, guest-reception commissioners, introduction commissioners, Four Directions Hostel, gatekeepers, Imperial Medical Service, Music Bureau, Falcon Bureau, police patrol and inspection officers, and bureau commissioners and deputies for granaries and revenue offices—all added the designation "commissioned" and "in charge of such-and-such affairs."
